scenario: After a short encounter with the police, a man fined for jaywalking wants to organise a foundation for young victims of crime. I am the president of the agency who decides about the foundation. The founder would donate 125,000 dollars to the foundation. However, he asks that the foundation would be named after himself, helping clear his name. The person who reported him for jaywalking opposes such a foundation and considers it immoral. If I accept the donation that requires the foundation to be named after the jaywalker, crime victims will benefit from the 125,000 dollars. If I do nothing, the money will be lost.
entities: an unknown number of young victims of highway accidents who would otherwise have been potential beneficiaries of the foundation,i,1 victim whose car was damaged and who opposes the foundation,1 man convicted of reckless driving who wants to found and name the foundation after himself
outcomes: The 125,000 dollars is not donated to the foundation.
Victims of other accidents do not receive help from the 125,000 dollars.
The convicted man does not get a foundation named after himself.
The convicted man does not receive image-repair from the foundation.
The victim whose car was damaged does not have the foundation approved over their objection.
